== Biography ==
Nathaniel Glasgow was baptised at Livingston on 2 January 1774, a son of [[Glasgow-1382|Thomas Glasgow]] and [[Davidson-14073|Christian (Christine) Davidson]]. The complete parental couple is named in both held parish-index derivatives.<ref name="Livingston1774">Findmypast, ''Scotland, Parish Births & Baptisms 1564–1929'', Nathaniel Glasgow, baptism 2 January 1774, Livingston, parents Thomas Glasgow and Christian Davidson; [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=R_685841078&tab=this R_685841078] and [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=R_692405171&tab=this R_692405171], inspected derivative transcripts retained from 30 October 2026; companion indexes of one baptism, original register uninspected.</ref> His existing birth bound is before 2 January 1774; no exact birthday is established. The father's identification with this Thomas/Christian adult household is assessed at 97% confident, separately from Thomas's own childhood and ancestry.

His later life and death remain unresolved. Nathaniel R. Glascoe of the 1799 Kingsessing committee and Nathan Glasgow, a Leith wright buried in 1835, remain possible comparisons; neither is identified as this Livingston child. No migration, trade, death, spouse or child attachment follows from those comparisons.

=== Possible Nathaniel R. Glascoe, Kingsessing committee ===
Nathaniel R. Glascoe is named in the Kingsessing township committee to act with the county committee and carry the preceding resolutions into effect.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/586545170/ Aurora General Advertiser, 1799-09-13, p.2].</ref>

The initial R. is recorded. The paragraph gives no age, family or origin. It does not by itself connect the committee member with either the Livingston Nathaniel or the Drumgreenagh farmer.

This may concern [[Glasgow-1452]]. Nathaniel’s birth before 2 January 1774 at Livingston is compatible with adult committee membership in 1799, but the Scottish parish entry gives no Philadelphia connection.
